title: 1c8mpx3
The Ayyam-i Fatimiyya
hook: Fadak was taken from her hand. A vow of fire was sworn before the door. She died in silence and her grave was hidden.
scenes.0.text: In Medina, after Saqifa, the grief of **Fadak** came. There were two claims. Hiba means gift. **Lady Fatima** said that the Prophet had given her the garden as a gift. The opposing claim was inheritance. Inheritance is the share that falls to an heir from the property of the deceased. The reply was short: "We prophets leave no inheritance." The garden was not given to her. The right was still hers. This grief did not end in the mosque. It continued afterward at the door of her house.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.1.text: In Medina, on the day of the bay'a, a group had gathered in **Imam Ali**'s house. **Umar** came to the door. He had had wood and fire brought. He said, "Come out, or I will burn the house down with those inside." When it was said, "Fatima is inside," **Umar** said, "Even so!" According to the report, he was one of those who set the door on fire. The house was **Imam Ali**'s house. The Prophet had taken his hand at Ghadir. The same door was threatened with fire.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.2.text: According to the narrations of the Ahl al-Bayt, the threat did not remain words. The door was set on fire and **Umar** forced it open by pushing it. **Lady Fatima**, standing behind the door, was crushed between the door and the wall. According to the narrations, the nail of the door pierced her chest and her rib was broken. At that moment she lost the baby she was carrying, named **Muhsin**. In pain she cried out, "O my father!" **Imam Ali** ran and lifted his wife from the ground. Muhsin, who never came into the world, lives in the hearts of the Shia as the first martyred child of the Ahl al-Bayt. These wounds turned the rest of Lady Fatima's short life into a sickbed.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.3.text: While **Imam Ali** was still at the side of his wounded wife, the crowd filled the house. According to the narrations, Imam Ali reached for his sword, but the men, who were many, moved before him and seized him. They bound his hands with a rope and dragged the Prophet's brother by force through the streets of Medina to the **Prophet's Mosque**, to make him pledge allegiance to Caliph Abu Bakr. Despite her pain, the wounded **Lady Fatima** rose, took **Imam Hasan** and **Imam Husayn** by the hand and walked after them with the women of Banu Hashim. As she neared her father's grave, she called out: "Let my cousin go! By God who sent my father with the truth, if you do not let him go, I will uncover my hair, place the shirt of the Messenger of God on my head and cry out to God." According to the narrations, as she was about to raise her hands for that curse, the walls of the mosque shook from their foundations. **Salman** hurried to her and said, "My lady, God sent your father as a mercy, do not become a cause of punishment." In the mosque, meanwhile, swords gleamed over Imam Ali and he was told, "Pledge allegiance, or we will strike your neck." Imam Ali reminded them of his right one by one and did not open his hand. According to the narrations, the Caliph passed his own hand over Imam Ali's clenched fist and contented himself with that.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.4.text: After this, in Medina, **Lady Fatima** did not speak with Caliph Abu Bakr. She was silent until her death. She was estranged from him. She lived six months after the Prophet. Fadak had been taken from her hand. The door had been broken. Her silence came from these two griefs.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.5.text: In the house in Medina, **Lady Fatima**'s days of illness grew long. These days are called the **Ayyam-i Fatimiyya**. **Imam Ali** did not leave her bedside. Little **Imam Hasan** and **Imam Husayn** stayed beside their mother. **Lady Fatima** kept her grief inside the house. The mourning that **Imam Hasan** and **Imam Husayn** would carry in the future began on this bed.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.text: Before her last breath, in the house in Medina, **Lady Fatima** left a bequest to **Imam Ali**. Those who had wronged her were not to come to her funeral. They were not to stand for her prayer. She was to be buried at night. Her grave was not to be known. With this bequest she carried her protest on to the grave. **Imam Ali** did not break this bequest.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.text: When **Lady Fatima** passed away, **Imam Ali** washed her at night in Medina. He performed her prayer himself. He buried her in the dark. He did not inform Caliph Abu Bakr. With him were the people of the house and a few close ones. By morning the body had been laid in the earth. At Saqifa this house had been left alone. At the farewell, too, there was no crowd.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.8.text: When the burial was finished that night, **Imam Ali** came to al-Baqi'. So that the place of **Lady Fatima**'s grave would not be known, he made the shape of several new graves. In the morning the people of Medina saw these new graves. The house, al-Baqi', and the space between the Prophet's grave and his pulpit are also mentioned as possibilities. There is no certain place.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.9.text: In the morning **Umar** and Abu Bakr came to al-Baqi'. **Umar** ordered: "Dig up the graves. Let us find Fatima and pray over her." The news reached **Imam Ali**. He came in anger. In his hand was Dhu al-Fiqar. He said, "If you move even one stone from her grave, this land will be watered with your blood." When **Umar** answered back, **Imam Ali** seized him by the collar. He shook him and struck him to the ground. Abu Bakr intervened: "O Abu al-Hasan, for the sake of the Messenger of God, let him go. We will do nothing that displeases you." When **Imam Ali** let go, they gave up searching for the grave. This is why **Lady Fatima**'s grave is still hidden today.
scenes.9.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.9.art.actors.1.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
sunni.0.says: Lady Fatima asks for the fay' in Medina, for Fadak, and for what remained of the khums of Khaybar. It is said, "We have no inheritance; what we leave is sadaqa." She becomes angry and does not speak until she dies. She lives six months. Imam Ali buries her at night, does not inform Abu Bakr, and performs her prayer.
sunni.1.says: From Zayd b. Aslam's father: Imam Ali and al-Zubayr gather at Fatima's house. Umar says he has sworn to have the house burned over them if they gather again. Fatima says: tell them inside and disperse.
sunni.1.grade: The text is widely transmitted; the page varies by edition, so it must be checked.
sunni.2.says: Al-Shahrastani transmits a saying of al-Nazzam of the Mu'tazila: Umar struck Fatima in the belly on the day of the bay'a, and she miscarried; he was shouting "Burn the house down with those inside"; in the house were Imam Ali, Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn. Al-Shahrastani calls this al-Nazzam's slander.
sunni.3.says: The threat of burning directed at those gathered in the house.
sunni.3.grade: The page was not read from the printed edition in this study.
sunni.4.says: Wood being brought and the words "Come out, or I will burn it down with those inside," and, when "Fatima is inside" was said, the answer "Even so."
sunni.4.grade: The attribution of the work to Ibn Qutayba is disputed. The page was not read in this study.
sunni.5.says: The inheritance claim over Fadak and Khaybar and the saying "prophets leave no inheritance." It is a parallel of the same report as Bukhari 4240.
sunni.5.grade: The number is a widely cited reference; the page was not opened in this round.
sunni.6.says: Lady Fatima was buried at night; the place of the grave is not known with certainty.
sunni.6.grade: The page was not read in this study.
sunni.7.says: After the cry at the door, Umar and those with him bring Imam Ali out of the house, take him to Abu Bakr and say "Pledge allegiance." When Imam Ali asks "What if I do not?", they say "By God, we will strike your neck."
sunni.7.grade: The attribution of the work to Ibn Qutayba is disputed. The Sunni mainstream does not accept this report.
shia.0.says: That Qunfudh struck Lady Fatima with a whip and its mark remained on her arm. In the al-Ihtijaj variant on the page it is also written that she was pushed against the door frame, her rib was broken and she miscarried. The attribution of the present copy of the book is also disputed among Shia rijal scholars.
shia.1.says: After the burial at night, there is a wish to disturb the grave. Imam Ali seizes the collar, lets him down on the ground, and says that blood will be shed if a stone is moved from the grave. Abu Bakr intervenes, and they disperse. The shape of several graves in al-Baqi', Umar's order to dig, and the saying "it will be watered with your blood" are in this report's narrative. No new page number was given. The footnote ties the report to Bihar al-Anwar 43/171.
shia.2.says: It is mentioned as the place where the grave scene in Dala'il al-Imama p. 137 was compiled. Several graves, Umar's order, Dhu al-Fiqar, seizing the collar and the saying of letting go as "Abu al-Hasan" are in this report. The volume of Bihar was not separately opened. No new page number was given.
shia.2.grade: The page was taken from the footnote of the Dala'il edition.
shia.3.says: The sermon Lady Fatima delivered in the mosque about Fadak is transmitted in this work.
shia.4.says: The bequest that those who wronged her not be present at the funeral and that the burial be secret.
shia.4.grade: The page was not read in this study.
shia.5.says: Three views about the place of the grave. No certain place is stated.
shia.5.grade: The page was not opened in this round.
shia.6.says: Umar asked for fire, brought it to the door and set the door on fire, then pushed the door. Lady Fatima met him. The sword in its sheath struck her flank, the whip her arm. The saying "Even so" is in the al-Imama wa al-Siyasa report. No new page number was given.
shia.7.says: Qunfudh whipped, Lady Fatima was squeezed against the door frame, pushed, her rib was broken and she miscarried.
shia.7.grade: The page was not opened in this round from the book's own edition; the sentence is transmitted through this page.
shia.8.says: The door is kicked. Lady Fatima has braced her body against the door. Then she leans on the wall and says that what is in her belly has died. Imam Ali gives the child that fell the name Muhsin.
shia.9.says: A late book. Here it is narrated that Umar squeezed Lady Fatima between the wall and the door, that she miscarried, and that the door nail pierced her chest.
shia.9.grade: A late source. The page is through the transmission of Ja'far Murtada al-Amili's Ma'sat al-Zahra.
shia.10.says: Imam Ali reaches for his sword; the crowd seizes him and ties a rope on him (the text says: they threw a rope around his neck; the al-Ihtijaj copy says a black rope). Lady Fatima comes between them at the door and Qunfudh whips her. Imam Ali is dragged by force to Abu Bakr. Lady Fatima cries out loudly, "O my father, O Messenger of God."
shia.10.grade: The text says the rope was thrown around his neck. The binding of the hands in the scene is a narrative choice.
shia.11.says: Imam Ali is brought before Abu Bakr in the mosque and reminds him of his right. Umar and Khalid b. al-Walid threaten to kill him if he does not pledge. Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn weep. Imam Ali argues three times, then stretches out his hand without opening his palm; Abu Bakr strikes upon it and is content with that.
shia.12.says: When Imam Ali is taken away, Lady Fatima comes out with the shirt of the Messenger of God on her head, holding her two sons by the hand. She says, "Were it not a wrong, I would uncover my hair and cry out to my Lord," and takes Imam Ali by the hand and leads him away.
shia.12.grade: The page was not opened in the book's own edition in this round; the text was read from a secondary quotation.
shia.13.says: Lady Fatima approaches the grave with the Hashimite women: "Let my cousin go, or I will uncover my hair, put the shirt of the Messenger of God on my head and cry out to God." Salman sees the walls of the mosque rise from their foundations and says, "God sent your father as a mercy, do not be a punishment." The walls return to their place.
shia.13.grade: The page is given via Ja'far Murtada al-Amili's al-Sahih min Sirat al-Imam Ali (vol. 9, p. 238); the book's own edition was not opened.
shia.14.says: Lady Fatima wants to go to the grave, uncover her hair and cry out to her Lord. Salman reaches her and says that Imam Ali has sent him to ask her to return home. Lady Fatima says, "Then I will return, be patient, listen and obey."
shia.14.grade: The page was not opened in this round; it was read from secondary quotations.
shia.15.says: Muawiya writes that Imam Ali was led to the pledge "like a camel with a nose-ring." Imam Ali replies: "You wanted to blame, but you praised; you wanted to disgrace, but you disgraced yourself. There is no shame for a Muslim in being wronged, so long as he has no doubt in his religion."
shia.15.grade: The letter text was read in several editions. The link is the text in al-Tustari's commentary Bahj al-Sabagha.
disputes.0.title: 1hishg5
The vow of fire and the door
disputes.0.sunni: The oath to burn the house is narrated in Ibn Abi Shayba and in other history books. Shahrastani also records al-Nazzam's statement about the blow and the miscarriage; he regards it as al-Nazzam's slander. Al-Imama wa al-Siyasa, attributed to Ibn Qutayba, writes that Imam Ali was taken out of the house and called to the pledge under threat of death.
disputes.0.shia: The oath to burn is written on both sides. The burning of the door is in Sulaym vol. 1, p. 387. Being crushed between the door and the wall, the nail and Muhsin are cited with Bihar vol. 30, p. 294 and Mu'tamar ulama' Baghdad p. 135. Imam Ali being bound after the door, dragged to the mosque and not opening his palm is in Sulaym vol. 1, p. 151 and p. 390. Lady Fatima warning them with a curse at the grave to save him is cited with al-Ihtijaj and Rawdat al-Kafi. These are narrations of the Ahl al-Bayt.
disputes.1.title: 118823v
Silence and the burial at night
disputes.1.sunni: Bukhari 4240 writes that she did not speak until her death and that Imam Ali buried her at night and did not inform Abu Bakr.
disputes.1.shia: The same sentence stands in Bukhari too. In the Shia reading, this is a bequest and a protest. Her grave was hidden for this reason.
questions.0: The Prophet had said, "Fatima is a part of me." Where does her silence hold love for the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.1: The vow before the door is written in the history of both books. While thinking of that threshold, what does patience tell you?
questions.2: Her grave is not known. How does a grave that is sought and not found keep the protest alive?
questions.3: While protecting the grave, Imam Ali had laid his own right on the ground. How does this patience describe his virtue to you?
summary: Fadak was refused. In the narration of the Ahl al-Bayt, Umar burned the door and kicked it in. Lady Fatima was caught between the door and the wall, her rib was broken and Muhsin was lost. Imam Ali's hands were bound and he was taken to pledge allegiance. Lady Fatima warned them with a curse to save him. She was buried at night. In the morning Umar wanted the graves dug up. Imam Ali stopped him with Dhu al-Fiqar. Her grave remains hidden today.
key: The Ayyam-i Fatimiyya: the door, Muhsin and the hidden grave
notes.0: The Fadak claim and the sermon in the mosque are tied to the day of the door.
notes.1: The vow to burn the house is also written in Sunni books (Ibn Abi Shayba; al-Shahrastani transmits al-Nazzam's saying, vol. 1, p. 57).
notes.2: According to the Ahl al-Bayt report, Caliph Umar burned and kicked the door (Sulaym, vol. 1, p. 387). Lady Fatima was caught between the door and the wall, her rib was broken, a nail pierced her chest and Muhsin fell (Bihar, vol. 30, p. 294).
notes.3: That she did not speak until her death and was buried at night is in Bukhari 4240.
notes.4: Imam Ali made the shape of several graves in al-Baqi'. In the morning Caliph Umar wanted to have the graves dug up. Imam Ali stopped him with Dhu al-Fiqar (Dala'il al-Imama, vol. 1, p. 137; Bihar 43/171). Her grave is hidden.
